purpose: Map public CC-Framework claims to evidence, validation lanes, supporting files, tests or commands, and explicit non-claims so that public communication remains evidence-bound.

claim_levels.C0: Repository Metadata Claim: basic facts about files, docs, package metadata, or repository organization.
claim_levels.C1: Structural Validation Claim: a schema, report, or artifact conforms to declared validation rules.
claim_levels.C2: Provenance / Integrity Claim: receipt-covered artifacts can be checked for byte integrity or tamper evidence under canonicalization and digest/signature verification.
claim_levels.C3: Mathematical Kernel Claim: a mathematical statement about finite binary atom spaces, Fréchet-Hoeffding bounds, identified intervals, endpoint witnesses, finite-sample outer intervals, or infeasibility detection under stated assumptions.
claim_levels.C4: Evidence-Governance Claim: a claim about how evidence roles, non-claims, freshness, confirmatory/exploratory boundaries, or governance checks are represented and validated.
claim_levels.C5: Deployment / Compliance Claim: out of scope for this repository unless a future release explicitly creates a separate authority layer. Current status: deferred / not claimed.

claims.claim_text: The strict kernel computes classical Fréchet-Hoeffding bounds for finite binary guardrail failure composition under exact singleton marginals and no additional side constraints.
non_claims: Does not prove marginals are representative.
claims.risk_if_overstated: Could be misrepresented as a safety certification or as evidence that exact singleton marginals identify the true deployment risk.

claims.claim_text: The finite atom LP computes sharp lower and upper values for declared linear composition queries over feasible finite binary atom distributions.
non_claims: Does not validate upstream data collection.
claims.risk_if_overstated: Could turn a conditional mathematical identification result into an unsupported empirical or deployment claim.

claims.claim_text: Under stated iid Bernoulli sampling assumptions and simultaneous moment coverage, count-derived LP intervals form an outer confidence interval for the target query.
non_claims: Not valid after uncorrected adaptive target selection.
claims.risk_if_overstated: Could imply finite-sample uncertainty handling proves future behavior or deployment safety outside the named assumptions.

claims.claim_text: Receipt/hash verification can provide tamper evidence for recorded bytes under canonical serialization and verification rules.
non_claims: Does not prove source data truth.
claims.risk_if_overstated: Could convert byte integrity or provenance into an unsupported empirical validity, compliance, or safety claim.

claims.claim_text: Documentation and reporting surfaces explicitly separate what each validation result supports from what it does not support.
non_claims: Does not prevent bad-faith actors from making misleading claims outside the framework.
claims.risk_if_overstated: Could imply documentation controls alone prevent institutional overclaiming or misuse outside the repository.

claims.claim_text: Paper Core v0.3 is release-candidate quality for the finite atom kernel, canonical metrics, endpoint witnesses, deterministic paper artifacts, and documentation spine.
non_claims: Does not promote enterprise, dashboard, vendor, cloud, or experimental lanes into paper core.
claims.risk_if_overstated: Could present a release-candidate paper-core boundary as whole-repository production quality.

claims.claim_text: Enterprise Reference v0.1 is an experimental evidence-integrity reference architecture with moto-backed smoke tests.
claims.risk_if_overstated: Could imply a moto-backed reference path is production infrastructure, live-cloud validation, compliance certification, or deployment safety.

claims.claim_text: The public research core is intended to remain inspectable for credibility and reproducibility, while possible private/commercial layers may operationalize the primitives.
non_claims: Does not make the project a product today.
claims.risk_if_overstated: Could turn a strategic boundary document into an unsupported claim that a commercial product already exists.

forbidden_upgrades.reason: Internal validation does not establish real-world safety.
Byte integrity and provenance do not establish sampling validity, measurement correctness, or inference quality.
Schema conformance checks structure, not whether the represented claim is true.
Review may satisfy a process requirement without adding new empirical support.
Exploratory findings require separate confirmatory design before being treated as proof.
A product baseline is a comparison calculation unless independence is separately assumed and supported.
A visual surface does not create certification authority.
Moto-backed or local smoke tests do not establish operational readiness.
Release-candidate status is scoped to the named paper-core lane.
A strategy document does not create product status.

global_non_claims: CC-Framework does not certify deployed AI systems.
CC-Framework does not prove regulatory compliance.
CC-Framework does not prove dataset representativeness.
CC-Framework does not prove deployment safety.
CC-Framework does not turn receipt integrity into statistical validity.
CC-Framework does not make schema validity equivalent to semantic truth.
CC-Framework does not claim enterprise readiness.
